name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Syntax-check every .cjs / .js
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          for f in **/*.cjs **/*.js; do
            case "$f" in node_modules/*) continue;; esac
            node --check "$f"
          done
      - name: Install (no secrets required)
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund || true
      - name: Test (runs against the zero-dependency echo path)
        run: npm test

🧩 Agent OS

A tiny, self-hostable operating system for autonomous agents: one kernel that routes each task to the right capability by KIND, runs work in cycles, and records everything — zero dependencies, $0 to run, bring your own models.
Most agent stacks hardcode a model name into every call site. Agent OS does the opposite. A capability is a seat — a logical slot like fast, reader, coder, or judge — and each seat self-reports the task KINDS it can serve. The router builds a by_kind index at runtime and resolves kind → capable seat on every task, so swapping providers, adding a local model, or wiring an MCP tool never touches your call sites. Around that router sits a kernel that runs a goal in cycles (classify → route → act → record → decide), a store that unifies memory, a durable ledger, and a live-state continuity snapshot in one JSONL-backed layer, and per-kind token budgets so a classification never burns a code-file allowance. It ships with a $0 deterministic echo adapter, so `node examples/demo.cjs` runs a full agent loop with no API key, no network, and no cost — then you drop in your own models behind the same seats. Zero dependencies. Nothing throws into your loop.

--- ## Why Agent OS Every agent framework eventually hits the same wall: the model name is glued to the call site. Change providers and you refactor everything; add a cheaper model for mechanical work and you thread a flag through ten functions; wire a new tool and your prompts break. Agent OS removes the glue. The unit of capability is a seat — a name you bind to whatever you run — and a seat declares the task kinds it can serve. The router keeps a by_kind index and answers one question at run time: do I have a capability for this kind? That single indirection is what lets a kernel stay identical while the models underneath change completely. On top of it, the kernel runs a goal as a short cycle loop and records every step to a durable ledger, the store carries live state across restarts so a fresh process resumes knowing what was mid-flight, and per-kind budgets keep fast work fast without starving reasoning. The whole thing runs for $0 out of the box on a deterministic echo adapter — you see a real agent loop execute before you spend a cent — and then you bring your own models behind the exact same seats. --- ## What it does | Module | What it does | Signal | |---|---|---| | **createRouter()** | Builds a by_kind index over seats and resolves kind → best capable seat at run time; unknown kinds skip-and-warn to a default seat instead of crashing | swap models, never touch call sites | | **createKernel()** | Runs a goal in cycles — classify → route → act → record → decide — and returns a full trace, scoreboard, and continuity block | a real agent loop, composable | | **createStore()** | One JSONL-backed layer for memory, a durable ledger, and a bounded live-state snapshot that survives process restarts | resume knowing what was mid-flight | | **echoAdapter() / bringYourOwn()** | A $0 deterministic provider so the demo runs with no key; bringYourOwn(fn, kinds) wraps any real model into a seat | $0 to try, yours to extend | | **createCatalog()** | A deduplicated registry of the capabilities the ecosystem ships — engines (runnable modules) and packs (templates, prompts, playbooks, checklists, tools) — each tagged by `kind` so it lines up with the router | one map of what the system can do | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD G["goal"] --> K["kernel.run()"] K --> C["classify → kind"] C --> R["router.route(kind)\nby_kind index → capable seat"] R --> S["seat.act(req)\nyour model, or the $0 echo adapter"] S --> M["store.remember + ledgerAppend"] M --> D{"resolved or maxCycles?"} D -- no --> C D -- yes --> O["trace + scoreboard + continuity snapshot"] classDef acc fill:#2e2952,stroke:#8B7CF6,color:#fff; class R acc; class M acc; ``` --- ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. run a full agent loop with NO api key, NO network, $0 (deterministic echo adapter) node examples/demo.cjs # 2. scaffold a config in your own project node bin/agent-os.cjs init # 3. run the kernel on your own goal node bin/agent-os.cjs run "Summarize the repository and propose the next improvement." # 4. read the scoreboard — cycles, kinds, success rate node bin/agent-os.cjs ledger # 5. browse the capability registry (optionally filter by kind) node bin/agent-os.cjs packs node bin/agent-os.cjs packs template ``` > Everything runs on the $0 echo adapter until you bring your own models. To wire a real model, register a seat: `router.register(bringYourOwn(async ({prompt}) => callYourModel(prompt), ['code','summarize'], 'coder'))`. Seats are names you choose; the router resolves task kinds to them. State lives under `./.agent-os` (memory.jsonl + ledger.jsonl). Nothing in the kernel ever throws into your loop. --- ## See it run

--- ## Capability registry The kernel routes by `kind`; the registry (`lib/catalog.cjs`) is the map of what capabilities exist to route *to*. Each entry is either an **engine** (a runnable module — a fusion engine, a memory, a router, a code-review pass) or a **pack** (a content/tooling capability — templates, prompt packs, playbooks, checklists, small tools), and every entry carries a `kind` so it lines up with a router seat. It is deduplicated: each capability appears exactly once. ```js const { createCatalog } = require('./lib/catalog.cjs'); const cat = createCatalog(); cat.count(); // total capabilities cat.engines(); // runnable modules cat.packs(); // content + tooling capabilities cat.kinds(); // every kind present, for wiring seats cat.byKind('template'); // capabilities that serve one kind cat.find('fusion'); // one entry by id ``` Extend it in-process — `createCatalog(extraEntries)` merges your own capabilities in — or edit the frozen `PACKS` list. The registry is pure data plus small pure query helpers, so it stays trivial to reason about and free to run. --- ## Repository layout ``` agent-os/ ├── bin/ │ └── agent-os.cjs ← CLI: init · run "" · ledger · packs ├── lib/ │ ├── router.cjs ← by_kind adaptive seat layer (the crown capability) │ ├── kernel.cjs ← the cycle engine: classify → route → act → record → decide │ ├── store.cjs ← JSONL memory + durable ledger + live-state continuity, one layer │ ├── adapters.cjs ← $0 echo adapter + bringYourOwn() for real models │ ├── budget.cjs ← per-kind token/effort budgets, floored │ └── catalog.cjs ← deduplicated capability registry (engines + packs), by kind ├── examples/ │ └── demo.cjs ← runs a full agent loop deterministically, $0, exits 0 └── .agent-os/ ← memory.jsonl + ledger.jsonl (gitignored, auto-created) ``` --- ## Concepts | Concept | Meaning | |---|---| | **Seat** | A logical capability slot — fast, reader, coder, judge — that you bind to any model. The router resolves task kinds to seats, so providers change and call sites do not. | | **by_kind index** | The runtime map of task kind → capable seats. # Agent OS — Architecture

Most agent stacks hardcode a model name into every call site. Agent OS does the opposite. A capability is a seat — a logical slot like fast, reader, coder, or judge — and each seat self-reports the task KINDS it can serve. The router builds a by_kind index at runtime and resolves kind → capable seat on every task, so swapping providers, adding a local model, or wiring an MCP tool never touches your call sites. Around that router sits a kernel that runs a goal in cycles (classify → route → act → record → decide), a store that unifies memory, a durable ledger, and a live-state continuity snapshot in one JSONL-backed layer, and per-kind token budgets so a classification never burns a code-file allowance. It ships with a $0 deterministic echo adapter, so `node examples/demo.cjs` runs a full agent loop with no API key, no network, and no cost — then you drop in your own models behind the same seats. Zero dependencies. Nothing throws into your loop.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    G["goal"] --> K["kernel.run()"]
    K --> C["classify → kind"]
    C --> R["router.route(kind)\nby_kind index → capable seat"]
    R --> S["seat.act(req)\nyour model, or the $0 echo adapter"]
    S --> M["store.remember + ledgerAppend"]
    M --> D{"resolved or maxCycles?"}
    D -- no --> C
    D -- yes --> O["trace + scoreboard + continuity snapshot"]
    classDef acc fill:#2e2952,stroke:#8B7CF6,color:#fff;
    class R acc;
    class M acc;
```

## How it fits together

Agent OS is a small set of pure-Node CommonJS modules with no dependencies. The router (lib/router.cjs) is the core idea: createRouter({ seats, defaultSeat }) indexes each seat by the task kinds it declares (a seat with kinds:'*' serves every kind) into a by_kind map, ordered by descending priority then registration order. route(kind) returns the best capable seat; when no seat is capable it warns and falls back to defaultSeat if configured, else throws a kind-named error — a forward-compatible skip-and-warn borrowed from production agent runtimes. Providers plug in behind seats via lib/adapters.cjs: echoAdapter() is a $0, keyless, fully deterministic act() function (classify hashes to a stable label, summarize returns a leading slice, code returns a stub), and bringYourOwn(fn, kinds, name) wraps any async model call into a seat. lib/budget.cjs maps kinds to floored max_tokens caps and an effort tier, with trim() applying a bytes/4 token estimate. lib/store.cjs unifies three concerns on JSONL: remember()/recall() over memory.jsonl, ledgerAppend()/scoreboard() over ledger.jsonl, and snapshot() — a bounded live-state block (cycle count, last goal, open work) that lets a fresh process resume. lib/kernel.cjs composes them: run(goal, {maxCycles}) loops classify → router.route → seat.act → store.remember + ledgerAppend → optional review → decide, capturing per-cycle errors into the trace so it never throws, and returns { goal, cycles, scoreboard, continuity }. bin/agent-os.cjs exposes init, run, and ledger; examples/demo.cjs runs the whole loop on the echo adapter and exits 0.

## Extending it

Every capability is a self-contained module. To add your own, follow the contract the existing
modules use and wire it into the entry point. Keep it portable — config via `.env`, no hardcoded
paths, no personal accounts.

## Design principles

1. **Route by capability, not by model name.** A seat is a logical slot you bind to any model; the router resolves task kinds to seats, so providers change and call sites don't.
2. **A goal is a bounded loop.** The kernel runs cycles until the work resolves — event-driven, never spinning, always returning a diffable trace.
3. **Continuity is a runtime property.** Live state lives on disk; a fresh process resumes knowing what was mid-flight instead of starting blind.
4. **$0 to try, yours to extend.** A deterministic echo adapter runs the whole loop with no key; real models drop in behind the same seats.
5. **Nothing throws into your loop.** Every layer is fail-open with bounded reads and atomic writes.

what it does

One kernel. Any models.

01 / ROUTE

Capability, not model name

A seat is a logical slot — fast, reader, coder, judge — that you bind to whatever you run. Each seat declares the KINDS it serves; the router builds a by_kind index and resolves every task to the best capable seat. Add a model, remove one, or wire a tool, and not a single call site changes.

02 / CYCLE

A goal is a short loop

The kernel classifies the goal, routes it, acts through the chosen seat, records the step to memory and a durable ledger, then decides whether to continue. Event-driven and bounded — it stops when the work resolves, never spins. Every run returns a diffable trace and a scoreboard.

03 / RESUME

State that outlives the process

The store keeps a bounded live-state snapshot — cycle count, last goal, open work — on disk. A fresh process reads it and resumes knowing what was mid-flight, instead of starting blind. Continuity is a property of the runtime, not something you bolt on.

Up and running in a clone.

Every value comes from .env. Nothing here is tied to any account — bring your own.

node examples/demo.cjs

# 2. scaffold a config in your own project
node bin/agent-os.cjs init

# 3. run the kernel on your own goal
node bin/agent-os.cjs run "Summarize the repository and propose the next improvement."

# 4. read the scoreboard — cycles, kinds, success rate
node bin/agent-os.cjs ledger
